techniques.use_when: A short browser flow is ready to rehearse and record.
techniques.usage: Import Demo into the task driver. Demo(session, scratch). Use run(*args) for native agent-browser commands, ready(expression) for UI state, and with record('take.webm', environment=observed) for capture. DEMO_BROWSER selects an executable. The context writes take.take.json when recorder startup or the flow fails and still raises the error. A startup failure has status failed and failure_stage recorder_start; video and capture_request describe the requested output and fps, not successful capture. Timing is null and events/recorder facts are empty until startup succeeds. If the diagnostic cannot be written, the startup error remains primary with the file error chained as its cause. Event times use the driver clock after the start response; the recorder starts asynchronously, so align visual actions before treating these as video timecodes. Establish the facts in references/capture-environment.md before app rehearsal/capture. Missing or blocked observations leave a failed take with failure_stage environment_check and no recorder call. New records include capture_request.environment and environment_check; legacy records remain valid.
techniques.limits: Requires agent-browser with record --fps and FFmpeg. Browser selection is DEMO_BROWSER first, then PATH discovery. DEMO_BROWSER accepts a runnable path or command name. Media tools use PATH. The retained successful Codex pilot resolved its Homebrew tools through PATH, so no fallback-only compatibility need was demonstrated; configure PATH explicitly on other hosts. No implicit installation-directory search. Fixed 30 fps request. Use a fresh session; record starts on the current page in tested version 0.37.1. No fixture reset or application-specific behavior. Environment eligibility uses supplied observations; it does not inspect banners, accounts, profiles or private data. A permitted decision applies only to the supplied target and is not reused implicitly.
techniques.check: python3 scripts/test_capture_environment.py -v checks supplied decisions and blocked recorder startup without a browser; python3 scripts/test_tool_selection.py -v checks tool selection with simulated paths; python3 scripts/test_helpers.py --record-only checks startup/success/error propagation without a browser; python3 scripts/preflight.py /absolute/new-scratch-directory --browser-profile-mode task_only checks actual capture.
techniques.tested_with: agent-browser 0.37.1; 0.27.3 produced 10 fps and is unsuitable for the default take

techniques.use_when: Typing, scrolling, or holds need a deliberate rhythm.
techniques.usage: type(selector, text, decisive=True) uses real key events and asserts the value. scroll_to(selector) waits for visible, settled motion. hold(seconds, target) records why the viewer is waiting. Fill unrelated fields before capture through run('fill', selector, text).
techniques.limits: Typing covers text inputs and textareas. CLI overhead bounds typing speed. Scroll targets must fit in the viewport. Use native driver commands for custom editors, drag gestures, or nested scrolling that needs special handling.

techniques.use_when: The changed field or result is easy to miss.
techniques.usage: Demo.focus(selector, color=None), then Demo.clear(). The standalone script also exposes window.__productDemo.focus and remove. It follows one live target and works inside modal dialogs. focus waits for finite ancestor entrance animations and confirms the ring has faded in before the reading hold begins.
techniques.limits: Requires native Popover API. Default color is #448fff, independent of application theme variables; an explicit CSS color overrides it. No captions, dimming, content replacement, or source edits. A hidden or detached target removes the ring.
techniques.check: python3 scripts/test_helpers.py --browser-profile-mode task_only checks default and explicit colors on an invented page with an app accent, saves rendered screenshots, and checks geometry, tracking, visibility, pointer noninterference, and cleanup.

techniques.use_when: Before a take with a recorder or capture setting not yet verified for this task.
techniques.usage: python3 scripts/preflight.py /absolute/new-scratch-directory --format mp4 --browser-profile-mode task_only. Match the planned take format: mp4 or webm (default). The fixture moves for two seconds, holds fully still for six seconds, then moves in green for two seconds. Retain preflight.media.json, preflight.motion.json, and preflight.fixture.json. Watch the entire preflight video at normal speed; reject it if the green dot does not move after the pause.
techniques.limits: Uses the capture helper at 1440 by 900. Decoded dot colors and positions catch missing motion after a hold and missing hold time; this check is specific to the fixture and does not certify source cadence or replace playback review. A nonzero exit rejects the selected capture setting. Confirm the task-specific action separately in rehearsal; the dot fixture does not verify typing, saving, or game-scene capture completeness. The caller must configure and verify the task-only profile; the profile-mode argument records that supplied observation and does not configure or inspect a browser. This trusted fixture never establishes the target app environment.
techniques.check: python3 scripts/preflight.py /absolute/new-scratch-directory --format mp4 --browser-profile-mode task_only, then python3 scripts/test_preflight.py /absolute/new-scratch-directory/preflight.mp4 /absolute/new-negative-control-directory. The test proves a frozen tail still passes media checks but fails the motion check.
techniques.tested_with: agent-browser 0.37.1; MP4/H.264 with real six-second idle hold; WebM/VP8 also selectable

techniques.use_when: A take or final encode is ready for review.
techniques.usage: python3 scripts/check_video.py demo.webm --expected-size 1440x900 --expected-fps 30 --min-duration 15 --max-duration 30 --max-bytes 10000000 Set limits from the brief. Use --audio-policy require for required sound; forbid is the silent default. --allow-audio remains an alias for --audio-policy allow. --h264-range-policy report (default) warns on full-range H.264; select reject-full-range when the delivery target's compatibility requirements exclude it.
techniques.limits: Requires ffmpeg and ffprobe on PATH; missing commands report how to supply them. Checks minimum picture presentation span (equality passes; omitted means no minimum), maximum container duration, decoded picture frame count against picture timing, dimensions, rate, size, and full video/audio decode. Reports raw pixel format and color range with known/unknown/missing statuses. Flags full-range H.264 under a documented delivery compatibility policy, without claiming a visible color defect. Reports separate picture and audio presentation intervals and rejects start, end, or duration mismatches beyond one video frame, accounting for codec padding. Does not judge meaningful audible content, listening quality, perceptual synchronization, pacing, legibility, privacy, or source cadence.
techniques.check: python3 scripts/test_check_video.py runs browser-free synthetic audio-policy, timing, minimum-duration, and color-reporting regressions. Also run the checker on the final reel and on a deliberately wrong expected size; the latter must exit nonzero.

techniques.use_when: Any reel is ready to deliver, including an edit of existing footage.
techniques.usage: Keep one evidence.json beside each reel in its own delivery folder. Fill version 1 with brief, provenance, capture/edit settings, referenced takes, clock-labelled beats, actual check reports, review/privacy coverage, limitations, reproduction and toolkit friction. Run python3 scripts/check_evidence.py <delivery>/evidence.json. After inspecting sheets and native frames, record per-decisive-beat findings with author/relay and sample references, and linked watch targets preserving final-output timing/precision. Run python3 scripts/review_delivery.py <delivery>/evidence.json <delivery>/handoff; include its watch list and a small review ZIP in the response. Inspect delivered beat/interval sheets and native frames for privacy concerns using the brief and known data provenance. Record privacy author/relay, inspected sample and sheet references, coverage and final-output finding times; see references/evidence.md#sampled-privacy-review.
techniques.limits: Python standard library only; no browser or media tools needed. Checks local structure, file identity and stated consistency, not decoding, clarity, privacy or publication fitness. Raw checks remain authoritative, including failures and warnings. Unknown clocks and edit maps stay unknown; no take-schema rewrite. Frame-review readiness is separate: missing/unreviewed/unresolved/not-visible decisive findings or unavailable/failing media checks produce diagnostic_only. Ready_for_review never establishes viewing, privacy or acceptance; structural validation permits truthful incomplete findings. Known privacy findings make the handoff diagnostic; unperformed/unavailable review stays prominently unreviewed. No-findings sample review can miss content between samples. The helper copies no media: preserve real flagged material locally and share only authorized material or a metadata-only diagnostic with omissions explained.
techniques.check: python3 scripts/test_check_evidence.py -v; validate the actual final delivery folder too. python3 scripts/test_review_delivery.py -v checks synthetic pixels, truthful diagnostic records, attribution and generated handoffs. python3 scripts/test_privacy_review.py -v checks supplied privacy findings, references/times, missing review and handoff preservation with invented media; it is not agent visual inspection.

techniques.use_when: A delivered encode needs inspectable beat frames and whole-reel interval samples.
techniques.usage: python3 scripts/beat_frames.py <delivery>/evidence.json <delivery>/frames-review writes a new index, timestamped sheets and full-resolution PNGs. Default mode both includes beat midpoints and two-second interval sampling. Use --mode beats or intervals, and --interval <seconds> when needed.
techniques.limits: Requires Pillow >= 10.1 and ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH. Uses final-output encoded times and decoded presentation intervals, retaining raw PTS and supplied precision/alignment. Never infers driver offsets, rewrites takes/maps/evidence, clamps out-of-range targets, or upgrades sampled material to viewing/privacy clearance. Unknown times remain unresolved. Exit 0 means extracted, 1 partial, 2 error; none certifies visual quality. Existing output directories are refused.
techniques.check: python3 scripts/test_beat_frames.py -v runs browser-free lossless numbered/color-coded frame tests, including exact/range boundaries, nonzero starts, variable frame spacing, missing output, edited clocks and inspectable sheet pixels.
